## Module 0 Question 1
# Task: Predicting student comfort with statistics using class experience
# Response: stat.comf
# Predictors: courses (PSTAT 115, PSTAT 160, PSTAT 171, PSTAT 175)

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
# Load data and select variables of interest
class_data <- read_csv('../data/background-clean.csv') %>% 
  select(response_id, stat.comf, courses)
head(class_data)
```
```{r}
# Summarize class dataset
summary(class_data)
```

```{r}
# Creating new columns corresponding to classes of interest
class_data <- class_data %>% 
  mutate(
    pstat_115 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 115'),1, 0),
    pstat_160 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 160'), 1, 0),
    pstat_174 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 174'), 1, 0),
    pstat_175 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 175'), 1, 0)
    )
head(class_data)
```
```{r}
# Summarize class data
class_totals <- class_data %>% summarize(across(c(pstat_115, pstat_160,
                                                pstat_174, pstat_175), sum)) %>% 
                pivot_longer(cols=everything(),
                             names_to = 'course',
                             values_to = 'total')
  
# Plot class totals
class_barplot <- class_totals %>% ggplot(aes(x=course, y=total)) +
  geom_col(fill = '#005A87') +
  labs(title = 'Students Per Upper Division PSTAT Courses',
       x = 'Course',
       y = 'Total Students') +
  theme_light()
class_barplot
```
From this plot, we can see that over half of the students who provided their survey data have taken one or both PSTAT 160 courses (34 students). Less than half of these students took PSTAT 174 (12 students), and less than a quarter of students took PSTAT 115 (7 students) and PSTAT 175 (6 students) respectively. 

```{r}
# Summarize Student Comfort
comfort_barplot <- class_data %>% ggplot(aes(x = stat.comf)) + 
  geom_bar(fill = ('#2E6F40')) +
  labs(title = 'Student Statistics Comfort Count',
       x = 'Comfort',
       y = 'Total')
comfort_barplot
```
```{r}
# Get totals
comfort_totals <- class_data %>% count(stat.comf)
comfort_totals
```

From this plot and the comfort totals, we can see that over half the students who provided their survey data reported they have 4/5 comfortability with statistics. Over a quarter of the students reported a comfortability of 5/5, while 9 students reported a comfortability of 3/5.
